title: Backend mid systemdesign notification service
question: Design a notification service that other internal services can call to send a user an email, SMS, or push notification.
idealAnswer:
Proposes a queue-based architecture: internal services enqueue a notification request and return immediately, a set of workers consume the queue and actually call the relevant provider (email/SMS/push), decoupling callers from provider latency and failures

Designs a reasonably provider-agnostic internal API/schema (recipient, channel, template, payload) so callers don't need to know provider-specific details, and providers can be swapped without changing callers

Handles provider failures with retries and backoff, and a dead-letter queue or failure table for notifications that repeatedly fail, rather than silently dropping them

Addresses idempotency/deduplication, e.g. a retry of the same enqueue request (or a caller's own retry) shouldn't result in the user getting the same notification twice

Considers user preferences and rate limits, e.g. not spamming a user with the same type of notification repeatedly, and respecting opt-outs, as a first-class part of the design rather than an afterthought
